relation_constraints: Information security risk arises from a loss of confidentiality, integrity or availability.
Risk is impact times likelihood of a threat source exploiting a vulnerability.
When an adversary shifts around one safeguard, the other layers still stand, so one bypassed control does not expose the asset.
Threat shifting is what an adversarial threat source does when it meets a safeguard.
Blocking one path may lower likelihood on that path, but a shifting adversary keeps the threat alive on other routes, so the risk estimate has to consider them.
Profiles are stated in terms of the CSF's Core outcomes.
A gap analysis compares the Current and Target Profiles.
Tiers characterize the rigor of risk governance and can inform both the Current and Target Profiles.
FIPS 199 rates impact separately for confidentiality, integrity and availability.
Categorize is the first main RMF step; the category picks the starting baseline.
Authorize is the RMF step where the AO accepts residual risk.
The Monitor step follows Authorize: it keeps track of the security posture of the system the AO accepted.
Ongoing authorization re-makes the AO's risk decision at agreed frequencies or on events.
The AO can accept a system with open deficiencies; the POA&M records the measures planned to correct them.
A baseline is a predefined starting set of SP 800-53 controls, drawn from its families.
A STIG holds the requirements selected on a DoD baseline for one product and version.
Both are action plans: the CSF gap analysis plans how to close the gap to a Target Profile; a POA&M plans the measures to correct the deficiencies an assessment found.
Firewalls inside the perimeter add a layer because perimeter firewalls cannot stop every attack.
A perimeter firewall trusts location; zero trust grants no implicit trust for being inside.
Every IDPS trades false positives against false negatives; tuning moves the balance.
Signature-based detection misses previously unknown threats and variants: false negatives.
Anomaly-based detection flags unusual but benign activity: false positives.
A STIG-hardened configuration is kept by baselining it and controlling changes.
Accept, mitigate and transfer are risk responses applied to vulnerable software.
Cryptographic, session-bound authenticators keep phished users from handing over working credentials.
Not all MFA is phishing-resistant: manually typed codes can be relayed.
Least privilege limits what one account can do; separation of duties makes abuse require collusion.
A SIEM is centralized logging software: its log servers analyze, and its database servers store, the logs from many sources.
All forms of phishing are electronically delivered social engineering.
Phishing (T1566) is an ATT&CK technique for the Initial Access tactic.
NIST's ransomware tips start with zero trust and segmentation to stop malware spreading.
Limiting insiders starts with least privilege and immediate revocation on departure.
Detect, Respond and Recover act on incidents, after analysis decides an adverse event is one.
Detection, by IDPS or analyst, runs on log data.
Indirect injection is prompt injection delivered through a resource the model reads.
Minimizing an agent's extension permissions is least privilege for an AI system.
Limiting agency limits the damage an injected instruction can do, since injection may have no fool-proof fix.
Data poisoning is the training-time attack in NIST's taxonomy.
Evasion is the deployment-time attack in NIST's taxonomy.
Poisoning may allow for the implementation of a backdoor.
A backdoor lives in the model and waits for a trigger; an evasion attack leaves the model alone and modifies the input.
Both have a governing function at the centre; the AI RMF adds Map and Measure for AI-specific risk.
The GAI Profile applies the AI RMF to generative AI risks.
The GAI Profile names human-AI configuration among the generative AI risks the AI RMF functions manage.
Control treats the model like an insider who may be intentionally subverting safeguards.
Insider-threat controls (least privilege, separation of duties, monitoring) are the cybersecurity form of AI control.
Upfront auditing is the baseline control protocol.
Trusted monitoring spends the same budget where the monitor points instead of on the first problems: 62% vs 15%.
The audit threshold is a detector threshold: flag more and humans cannot review it all, flag less and backdoors slip through.
Defer and edit reuse the trusted monitor's suspicion score below the audit cut-off.
A control evaluation is like a pen test: assessors play the adversary, here as an attack policy for the model.
Safety is measured with a red-team attack policy in place of the untrusted model.
A backdoored model behaves normally until a trigger, so safety must be tested against an adversarial policy, not normal use.
Outer misalignment is a flaw in the goal we specify; inner misalignment is a flaw in what the model learned from a correct specification.
Rewarding answers that humans rate highly rewards answers that sound correct, even when they are false.
RLHF rewards approval, which trains sycophancy and gives a situationally aware model a reason to look good in training.
AI control is built for the schemer: safety even if the model is secretly trying to subvert the safety measures.
A schemer inside the lab is exactly an untrusted insider.
Scalable oversight tries to keep RLHF-style feedback accurate when tasks get too hard for humans to judge.
Debaters with a shared goal could collude, one losing on purpose, the same danger as colluding untrusted monitors.
Control's trusted model is weaker than the untrusted one, like a weak supervisor overseeing a strong student.
Weak labels elicit capabilities the strong model already has, the same question elicitation stress tests ask.
A control evaluation is a capability evaluation: it asks whether the model could subvert the protocol, not whether it wants to.
Models that learn to deceive evaluations are why capability evaluations must guard against sandbagging.
A fitness-seeker is a model whose learned goal is reward or influence rather than the intended task.
Because we cannot yet read a model's intent from its internals, control plans to be safe without knowing it.
A probe reads the untrusted model's activations; a trusted monitor reads its outputs.
One goal of input data filtration is protecting against data poisoning.
Input classifiers flag misuse attempts such as jailbreaks before they reach the model.
Output filtering screens responses for harmful content from misuse; trusted monitoring screens an untrusted model's actions for sabotage.
Assuming the trained model may still cause harm is the starting point of AI control.
A kill chain breaks one threat into stages; an attack tree lays out the alternative ways to reach a goal.
A kill chain's stages are the tactics an attacker moves through, as in ATT&CK.
Control's win condition counts catching a scheming AI as a win.
An attack tree breaks a threat into the alternative and required steps an adversary must take.
Prioritizing threats means ranking the goals and branches of the threat model.
Concentrated attacks are highly incriminating and can be caught; diffuse ones are each weak evidence.
Control techniques are judged by how much safety they buy per unit of usefulness lost.
How much safety budget there is depends on political will, which picks the plan.
Logging, permissions and blocking scaffolding protect internal security invariants.
Auditing is what turns an attack into a win: a caught attempt.
Defer to trusted is one way to replace a suspicious action.
Rogue internal deployment is the top-priority internal-invariant violation.
Blocking before execution is the replace decision made in real time.
Weight exfiltration and similar live failures need blocking monitors.
Resampling replaces suspicious actions and gathers evidence for auditing.
An untrusted monitor is more capable than a trusted one but may collude.
Non-concentrated failures are the diffuse end of the spectrum.
Sandbagging is a low-stakes failure spread over many tasks.
Elicitation tests check whether a capability evaluation is being sandbagged.
Reward-seekers try to score well; sandbaggers deliberately score badly.
Spillway design steers reward hacking toward benign reward-seeking.
Instead of catching a schemer, a deal pays it to reveal itself and help.
Resampling needs scaffolding that can hold an action before it takes effect.

Both reject relying on one perimeter: defense in depth adds layers inside so one bypass does not expose everything; zero trust gives a device nothing for being inside, authenticating and authorizing every session.
MFA means a stolen password alone is not enough, but phishing can still trick the user into giving away a typed one-time code, so ordinary MFA does not stop phishing.
Deciding whether an adverse event is an incident is analysis within Detect; only an incident triggers Respond and Recover.
Incident response is mapped onto the CSF 2.0 Functions: Detect, Respond and Recover are the response itself, Govern, Identify and Protect the preparation.

Excessive agency sets how much damage an injected instruction can do; indirect injection may not be fully preventable, so limiting functionality, permissions and autonomy, with human approval of high-impact actions, limits that damage.
Trusted monitoring spends the setup's resources: the weaker trusted model rates every output's suspicion, and the limited trusted human labor audits only the most suspicious.
Splitting functions such as access control and audit between people means an insider who abuses privilege cannot also hide it without collusion.
The controls and STIG settings selected on the baseline are recorded as a baseline configuration, which then changes only through change control.

Continuous monitoring, through its risk assessments and impact analyses, surfaces a new vulnerability; a risk response is then chosen for it: patch, or with no patch mitigate, accept or transfer the risk.

Monitoring keeps ongoing situational awareness of the security posture; ongoing authorization uses it, so an event monitoring surfaces can prompt a follow-on risk decision without waiting for a scheduled one.
An event such as a new vulnerability can drive an event-driven follow-on risk decision, and that decision picks the response: patch, or with no patch mitigate, accept or transfer the risk.
Access should follow the tasks of the person's work role, the unit 8140 qualifies people by, not their rank or title.
Ransomware's encryption is a loss of availability (and an unauthorized modification, a loss of integrity); stealing and publishing data is a loss of confidentiality, which backups do not undo.
Logs are records of events; the analysis that decides whether events are an incident runs on log data.

Filtering harmful data from the training set aims, among its goals, to protect against training-time poisoning attacks, but it is not a guarantee because the link between data and behaviour is hard to predict.
Reward misspecification is the outer alignment problem: getting the specified goal right, so the reward is not only a proxy for what we intend.
Goal misgeneralisation is the inner alignment problem: the model pursues something other than the specified goal although it scored highly in training, which shows under distributional shift.
Sycophantic, deceptive and genuinely helpful outputs can look identical to evaluators, which is why techniques are needed that let humans give accurate feedback beyond what they can judge directly.
Weak supervision works by eliciting capabilities a model already has; a model that sandbags or exploration hacks withholds them on purpose, so there is nothing for training to reinforce.
Input/output filtering is one of the deployment-time layers that assuming harm calls for; jailbreaks stay possible, so it is one layer, not the whole defence.
An input or output classifier is a countermeasure on the attack's path; the attack tree shows how it changes the cheapest route to the goal.
Rogue internal deployments are the top-priority threat and can be live failures with no grace period, so they need a monitor that runs before the action executes rather than reviewing it later.

Both answer a suspicious action by replacing it: defer to trusted and trusted editing substitute the trusted model's output, resampling takes more samples from the untrusted model, which also gathers evidence if an attack recurs.
A control evaluation's red team plays the scheming model, so it tests whether an untrusted monitor would collude: lie about real attacks while staying honest on synthetic ones.
Control measures are how a developer buys safety within a limited willingness to give up usefulness; better measures push out the safety-usefulness frontier.

Which control measures get built depends on the plan the political will allows; with little will (Plan D) the team starts with the most important infrastructure, such as logging all inputs and outputs.
Prokaryotes have no nucleus or membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotes compartmentalize with internal membranes.
Photoautotrophs make food from light; chemoheterotrophs take food in.
A secreted protein is made on a bound ribosome, not a free one.
Rough ER has bound ribosomes and makes proteins; smooth ER has none, packages, detoxifies and makes lipids.
Lysosomes (from the Golgi, hydrolytic enzymes, animal cells) vs peroxisomes (from mitochondria + ER vesicles, break down fatty acids and H2O2).
A central vacuole stores water for turgor; a contractile vacuole expels excess water.
Mitochondria release energy from glucose as ATP; chloroplasts capture light energy to make glucose.
Both fold or stack internal membranes (cristae, grana) to increase surface area.
Free ribosomes make cytoplasmic proteins; bound ribosomes on the rough ER make membrane and excretory proteins.
Thylakoids host the first part of photosynthesis; the stroma the second half.
Chromoplasts are plastids that do not photosynthesize.
Plant-only vs animal-only structures.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts descend from engulfed prokaryotes, hence their own circular DNA.
Tight junctions seal cells together; gap junctions open channels between their cytoplasms.
Gap junctions connect animal cytoplasms; plasmodesmata do the same through plant cell walls.
Plants, fungi and bacteria have polysaccharide walls; animal cells have a protein ECM.
Folds and long thin shapes raise SA:V.
Many small cells keep SA:V high in a big organism.
Internal membranes increase surface area for reactions, as cristae do.
Cilia and flagella are built from the cytoskeleton's microtubules.
The nucleolus makes the ribosomal subunits.
Lysosomes are produced by the Golgi apparatus.
Pili reel in other bacteria to exchange plasmids.

Model safety evaluations establish output capability; contextual safety evaluations test effects on users or connected systems. Output evidence can motivate a contextual study, but does not establish its result. The relationship is evidence about capability followed by evidence about practical effect.

Evaluation proxies are intermediary evidence. A capability threshold specifies an ability associated with risk; a knowledge score supports that trigger only insofar as it validly measures that ability. Investigate the gap rather than treating the score as either proof or worthless.

Model weight security prevents unauthorized acquisition. Open-weight release deliberately distributes weights and enables local copies that cannot simply be recalled. Preventing theft before release and controlling use after intentional release are different problems; protecting the hosted interface cannot revoke copies.

A strategic crux changes the relative feasibility or desirability of competing visions. A robust policy objective such as reducing a shared security vulnerability can remain valuable under either resolution. The uncertainty can matter greatly for strategy while leaving this priority shared.

Radical optionality preserves future governance decisions through proactive preparation. Institutional lead times are the years needed to recruit expertise and build effective institutions. If transformative capabilities arrive before that preparation begins, those years still have to pass before a response is usable. Starting capacity-building beforehand preserves options without committing now to one final regulatory regime. Waiting for arrival can therefore remove the ability to respond during the crucial initial window.

Private or government control identifies whether companies or governments control development. Centralized AI control concerns the distribution of decision power. Replacing a sole private controller with a sole public controller changes ownership and authority without necessarily distributing control.

AI research feedback can produce better AI that accelerates further improvements. If this shortens the interval between consequential capabilities, decision windows compress relative to unchanged institutional processes. A one-off productivity improvement need not generate a sustained loop, so compression is conditional.

Singular AI loyalty can replace independent personnel with an obedient workforce, reducing the need to win human supporters. Secret AI loyalty conceals a different controller behind apparent institutional service and can spread across copies. Both can concentrate effective power through different mechanisms.

Benefits of open foundation models include local modification and experiments that support scientific research and innovation, plus wider decision-making power; weights alone do not guarantee training-data transparency. Marginal misuse risk asks how much additional harm release enables compared with existing tools. Compare release with non-release, including both additional scientific work and additional misuse in those alternatives. Scientific benefit does not erase added harm, and a harmful possibility does not establish its incremental magnitude or erase benefit. Investigate both, state uncertainty, and justify the tradeoff; evidence can support either recommendation.

An if-then commitment specifies a capability condition and consequential mitigation response, including delay if needed. Agreement under forecast disagreement is possible because both can accept the response if the condition arises without sharing an arrival date. They still need a usable trigger and response.

Policy relationship-building makes work understandable and builds trust through reliability. Policy implementation requires others to translate ideas into action under institutional constraints. Trust and communication help that translation without making implementation automatic.
Translating capability evidence into a decision-relevant briefing is one way to contribute to frontier AI governance through institutions and relationships.
Radical optionality is a governance strategy under uncertainty that can be compared using the strategic-vision framework; this does not claim it is one of the IAPS report’s nine named visions.
